behavior.int_formatter: 0x61d0940 formats a long as "%li" (|n| <= 9999), "%liK" (n/1000, |n| <= 9999999), "%liM" (n/1e6, |n| <= 9999999999), "%liG" (n/1e9), with truncating signed division by magic multiply (0x20c49ba5e353f7cf>>7, 0x431bde82d7b634db>>18, 0x112e0be826d694b3>>26; verified equal to truncating division on 20000 random values per band). INT64_MIN takes the plain path (its absolute value stays negative, which is <= 9999 signed).
behavior.label_argument: the row's first %s is *(rsi): the caller passes a std::string whose data pointer is its first qword. The four observed calls pass "L" + decimal(level), "Sum", "Int", and a priority name (Bottom/Low/High/User/Invalid).
behavior.output: one data row written into the caller's character buffer (the big dump caller's stack buffer at rsp+0x4c0, 2024 bytes) with a single __snprintf_chk call on a 2000-byte budget (maxlen 0x7d0, flag 2, slen -1); the caller appends the buffer to its output string with string::append(const char*) after each call.
behavior.size_conversion: key 3 (SizeBytes) is converted to an unsigned long before the human-size call: below 2**63 plain cvttsd2si; at or above 2**63 subtract 2**63, convert, and flip bit 63 (0x5eedc70: subsd, cvttsd2si, btc $0x3f). NaN takes the plain path and yields INT64_MIN; value >= 2**64 yields 0 after the bit flip; a negative long reaches the human-size formatter as its unsigned bit pattern.
behavior.snprintf_budget: one __snprintf_chk call (0x5eedc20) with maxlen 2000: it writes at most 1999 characters plus the terminating NUL and reports the would-be length. The row's fixed widths sum to 192 characters including the newline when the human-size string fits its %8s field; a longer size string (e.g. "117.74 MB", 9 characters) makes the row longer.
behavior.throw: any looked-up key missing from the double map throws __throw_out_of_range("map::at") at 0x4408a7, either from the accessor 0x5eebac0 or from one of the seven inlined finds' jumps to the throw blocks (0x5eedd18, 0x5eedd37, 0x5eedd56, 0x5eedc90, 0x5eedcb3, 0x5eedcd6, 0x5eedcf9).

columns.derivation: The 14 map::at (accessor 0x5eebac0) calls pin keys 21, 20, 19, 18, 16, 14, 13, 10, 9, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3. The 7 inlined lower_bound + equality lookups pin keys 17, 15, 12, 11, 8, 2, 1: each loop compares against key-1 with jle (lower_bound(key)) and the check compares against key with jg to a throw block, so the accepted key is exactly the check constant (key 1's loop compares against 0 with test/jg). The 8 xmm varargs are keys 4..11 in order; the 13 stack varargs are pushed in reverse order, so the row order is the label (r9 = *(rsi)) followed by keys 1..21. verify.py re-derives this order from main.txt.
columns.header_correspondence: The header row (PR #3180, format at 0x9572f8) has 21 columns: label + the pair map's SECOND strings for keys 1, 3..21. The data row has 22 fields: the %6d/%-3d pair (keys 1 and 2) shares the header's single "Files" column, and the other 19 metric fields sit under the header columns for keys 3..21. The header row is 192 characters including the newline.

context_map.names_source: the metric names (FIRST strings) and header display names (SECOND strings) are the global pair map's entries, keys 1..21, derived from the static initializer 0x5efbd80 and recorded in PR #3180's packet (research/work-items/RE-001-compaction-stats-header-115/records.json, pair_table); the row formatter itself never reads the pair map, it reads the per-level double map.
context_map.type: the formatter reads a std::map<int, double> (header 32 B at map+0x08: color, parent at +0x10, left, right; node count at +0x28; node key at +0x20, double value at +0x28)

accessor.note: std::map<int, double>::at: lower_bound(key) + equality check; returns &value (the double) and throws __throw_out_of_range("map::at") when the key is missing. 14 call sites, all inside the formatter (exhaustive census).

formatter.returns: void (writes into the caller's buffer; rax is 0 on return)
formatter.signature: f(out=rdi: char*, label_ptr=rsi: std::string*, metrics=rdx: std::map<int, double>*; rcx ignored)

humansize.note: formats a long (treated as an unsigned 64-bit value via the negative path) as "%.2f KB|MB|GB|TB": value = (double)u, multiply by 1/1024 until below 1024.0. 4 call sites in the binary: 1 here (0x5eedac6) and 3 in the stats-snapshot consumer 0x5eefda0 (0x5eefe27, 0x5eefe65, 0x5ef009c).

intfmt.note: formats a long into a std::string as "%li" / "%liK" / "%liM" / "%liG" by |n| bands with truncating magic division. 12 call sites: 2 here (0x5eed76c, 0x5eed796) and 10 in one other routine at 0x5ef5314..0x5ef5795 (not examined here).

label_assign.note: std::string::assign(const char*): assigns a .rodata literal to a std::string. Re-shipped byte-identical from PR #3180's packet (string_assign.txt). Used by the big dump caller to set the label strings ("Level" 0x5ef6736, "Sum" 0x5ef6dfb, "Int" 0x5ef7064, "Priority" 0x5ef7114).

node_create.note: creates a fresh 0x58-byte outer-map node (operator new 0x58): key at +0x20, inner map header at +0x28 (color 0, parent 0, left 0, right = &header, count 0 -- an empty inner map), then _Rb_tree_insert_and_rebalance and the map count++. 4 call sites: 0x5ef1e9f, 0x5ef262e (unexamined routines), 0x5ef722b (Sum create), 0x5ef72ba (priority create).

outer_insert.note: inserts metric ids 1..21 from one 192-byte level struct into an inner map<int, double> (see PR #3164). 4 call sites: 0x5ef1e2a, 0x5ef23b4, 0x5ef25bc, 0x5ef70d0 (the Int row's map).

priority_name.note: assigns the priority name for a key into a std::string via 0x5fcd890: 0 Bottom, 1 Low, 2 High, 3 User, else Invalid. 2 call sites: 0x5ef72cd (site 4) and 0x61d5115 (unexamined).

unknowns: The 192-byte priority-aggregate struct at rsp+0x1f0 that outer_insert turns into the Int row's map is computed by the vectorized block at 0x5ef6e47..0x5ef7050 (including a ratio divsd at 0x5ef704c); its fields are not pinned here.

The sibling 0x5ef1d60 (FDE 0x5ef1d60..0x5ef1f39) that builds the priority outer map, and the filler 0x5ef1fa0 that rebuilds the level outer map, are not pinned beyond their call sites; whether the priority map always contains every key the site-4 loop asks for (which would make the node_create path dead code) is not established.

The Sum and priority create paths call node_create, which initializes an EMPTY inner map; a row printed from it would throw map::at on key 21, so those paths either never run in practice or abort the dump -- not resolved here.
The second lower_bound walk in the site-4 loop (0x5ef725f..0x5ef729b) duplicates the first walk's key search; its exact role (insert-hint computation for the create path) is inferred, not proven.
The int formatter's 10 other call sites (0x5ef5314..0x5ef5795) and priority_name's other caller (0x61d5115) belong to routines not examined here.

The formatter's buffer is the caller's 2024-byte stack buffer; the formatter's own writes never pass offset 2000, but the caller's buffer size is inferred from the frame layout (0xca8 - 0x4c0), not from a stated allocation.
What object *(owner+0x788) points to and what its +0x08 char* names (the header formatter's title argument) is not pinned in this packet; the row formatter does not use it.
